newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thailand to seek flexibility over IT at WTO meet.
newsitem.headline: Thailand to seek flexibility over IT at WTO meet.

text.p: Thailand will ask for flexibility over the proposed liberalisation of information technology (IT) industry at the upcoming World Trade Organisation Ministerial Conference in Singapore, a senior commerce ministry official said on Wednesday.

Karun Kitistaporn, head of the ministry's business economics department, said Thailand needs room for further negotiation on the time frame, the type of products to be liberalised and the level of tariff reduction.
"We agree in principle that the IT industry should be liberalised. But developing countries like Thailand need some flexibility," he told reporters.
WTO chief Renato Ruggiero has said he hopes to see a global accord on scrapping tariffs on information technology products at the December 9-13 meeting.

The United States has set an IT accord as its own top priority at the meeting. The accord proposes to remove all duties on computer hardware and software, semi-conductors and telecommunications equipment by the year 2000.
Analysts say an agreement along these lines would open up trade worth over $400 billion a year.
Karun also said that the establishment of a new Thai government on December 1 made it difficult to make quick commitments.
He said Thailand will push for room in the accord which would allow any country that does not endorse the accord to negotiate further.

A team of IT experts has been set up to study the impact of liberalisation on each product, he said. The study is expected to be concluded by March 1997. "We hope to use the paper as a basis for negotiation," he said.

Karun also said Thailand will strongly oppose any effort to link labour to trade. "Most developing countries believe the issue should be left in the hands of (The International Labour Organization)," he said.
